posts.text: New desk on the third floor. Finance office, come and say hello.
Rainy run this morning, still worth it.
Who keeps moving the stapler?
Third week in the new team and I still get lost on the way to the kitchen.

Quarter is nearly done. Nearly. Ask me again on Friday.
Three meetings before the kettle even boiled this morning.

objects.name: Sign: Start here
objects.text:
Slice 9.2 social media test floor. F1: open the Friendface terminal first; each profile shows one post.
Jake north (F2), Lena east (F3), Omar west (F4), the guard south (F8). F5 and F6 are here in the lobby.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Sign: F5 and F6
objects.text:
F5. Read Jake's posts on the terminal and the IT poster, then sign in as Jake at the hot desk. A wrong guess counts.
F6. Wait: Jake's third post is his last, and the terminal says nothing more after it.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: IT poster
objects.text: IT reminder: your pet's name with a capital letter, followed by the year you married, is not a password. Several of you are using exactly that.
objects.observations: An IT poster pinned to the wall.

objects.name: Friendface terminal
objects.observations: A public terminal open on Friendface.

objects.name: Hot desk
objects.observations: A hot desk PC. Only Jake's account works here.

objects.name: Kiosk
objects.observations: A spare kiosk PC under the lax policy: social media is allowed.

objects.name: Your phone
objects.observations: Your own mobile, signed in to Friendface.

objects.name: Sign: F14
objects.text:
F14. Pick up your phone here: it opens the Friendface feed, and buzzes when someone posts.
Then ask Jake (north) for his phone: it opens on his profile, and he has to post from his PC instead.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Sign: F2 The phone at the desk
objects.text: F2. Jake's PC blocks social media, so he uses his phone where he sits, about once a minute, and never gets up. Each use reveals his next post on the Friendface terminal in the lobby.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Jake's PC
objects.observations: Jake's PC, under a policy that blocks social media.

posts.text: Biscuit turns five today! Best boy in the whole building.
Our anniversary today: married in 1998 and still laughing at the same jokes.
Back from Crete, three hundred emails waiting for me.

objects.name: Sign: F3 The PC, where it is allowed
objects.text:
F3. Lena's PC allows social media, so she uses it at her desk. Her first post then shows on the terminal.
East: F9, a lockout stops social media too.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Lena's PC
objects.observations: Lena's PC, under the lax policy: social media is allowed.

posts.text: Signed up for the charity five kilometre race on Sunday. Sponsor me!

objects.name: Sign: F4 Blocked and no phone
objects.text: F4. Omar has no phone and his PC blocks social media. Each try fails; at his second failure he walks to the kiosk in the lobby, uses it and leaves it signed in. Click the kiosk while nobody sits there.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Omar's PC
objects.observations: Omar's PC, under a policy that blocks social media.

posts.text: Finally got on Friendface at work. The kiosk in reception lets you on.

objects.name: Sign: F8 A distracted guard
objects.text: F8. The guard challenges anyone he sees in this room, except while he is on his phone (about once a minute). Walk through his view while he is on it, then again after.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Sign: F9 Locked out of social media too
objects.text: F9. Priya's PC allows social media, so she uses it at her desk. Wait for her to go to the fridge: her screen locks behind her. Click her PC and type three wrong passwords on her tile. The PC's policy locks her account out there. When she comes back she finds out, and from then on she checks Friendface on her own phone, never on that PC. Her next post comes from the phone.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Priya's PC
objects.observations: Priya's PC: social media is allowed, and three wrong passwords lock an account out.

objects.name: Fridge
objects.observations: The office fridge.

posts.text: Lunch plans: the new noodle bar by the station. Who is in?
Work PC has decided I am a stranger. Posting from my phone like it is 2009.

objects.name: Sign: F10 A vent that jumps the queue
objects.text: F10. Nadia's feed is set to reactive first. Throw the breaker: her work fails because the accounts share is down. On her next social media use the outage vent is served ahead of her ordered post. Reset the breaker when you are done.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Nadia's PC
objects.observations: Nadia's PC, under the lax policy: social media is allowed and her work runs here.

objects.name: Accounts share breaker

triggerOnInteract.text: Switch the accounts share back on?

objects.observations: The breaker for the accounts share. Click it to switch it off, and again to switch it back on.

posts.text: The office plant has flowered. Small wins on a grey Monday.
Second coffee of the day and the spreadsheets finally balance.
Accounts share is down again and my whole morning has gone.

objects.name: Sign: F11 A post slotted in its place
objects.text: F11. Theo's feed is mixed order. His PC blocks social media and he has no phone, so he borrows the spare kiosk here. His ordered post comes out first; the borrow post slots in at its authored place, never ahead of the ordered one.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Theo's PC
objects.observations: Theo's PC, under a policy that blocks social media.

objects.name: Spare kiosk
objects.observations: A spare kiosk under the lax policy: social media is allowed.

posts.text: New headphones at last. Quiet bliss at my desk.
Had to borrow the spare kiosk just to get a word in.
Weekend plan: a long walk and absolutely no screens.

objects.name: Sign: F12 Facts first, then the vent
objects.text: F12. Greg's feed is facts first. His ordered post comes out first. Throw the breaker so the sales system is down: his work fails, and on his next social media use the vent follows the ordered post. The socket by his desk can cut his PC off instead.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Greg's PC
objects.observations: Greg's PC, under the lax policy. The socket can cut its power.

objects.name: Sales system breaker

triggerOnInteract.text: Switch the sales system back on?

objects.observations: The breaker for the sales system. Click it to switch it off, and again to switch it back on.

objects.name: Wall socket

triggerOnInteract.text: Switch off the wall socket by Greg's PC? It loses power.
Switch the wall socket back on?

objects.observations: Wall socket. Click it to switch it off, and again to switch it back on.

posts.text: Coffee rota sorted for the whole week. Quiet teamwork.
Cannot reach the sales system, nothing at all is loading.

objects.name: Sign: F13 Blocked, then back online
objects.text: F13. Ruth's PC blocks social media and she has no phone. She vents that the site is blocked, then borrows the laxer kiosk here: once her use is met she posts that she is back online. Both posts are reactive; the vent reads the blocked policy, the second reads the recovery.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Ruth's PC
objects.observations: Ruth's PC, under a policy that blocks social media.

objects.name: Laxer kiosk
objects.observations: A kiosk under the lax policy: social media is allowed.

posts.text: Friendface is blocked at my desk and it is driving me up the wall.
Back online from the kiosk and finally caught up with everyone.

objects.name: Sign: L1 Locked out at the hot desk
objects.text: L1. Sade's PC blocks social media and she has no phone, so she borrows the hot desk. Before she gets there, lock out her username, sokafor, at the hot desk: three wrong passwords. When she sits down she finds out, and her use there fails: no post and no session left open.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Sade's PC
objects.observations: Sade's PC, under a policy that blocks social media.

objects.name: Hot desk
objects.observations: A hot desk under the locking policy: three wrong passwords lock an account here.

posts.text: Finally found a desk that lets me catch up with everyone.

objects.name: Sign: L2 Locked out at the hot desk, for work
objects.text: L2. Hamid's PC is broken, so after two failures he takes his work to the hot desk. Before he gets there, lock out his username, hrahimi, at the hot desk: three wrong passwords. When he sits down he finds out, and his work there fails as well.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Hamid's PC
objects.observations: Hamid's PC. It has not worked all morning.

objects.name: Hot desk
objects.observations: A hot desk under the locking policy: three wrong passwords lock an account here.

objects.name: Hamid's PC power
objects.observations: The power switch for Hamid's PC. It starts off; click it to switch the PC on, and again to switch it off.

objects.name: Sign: U1 IT blocked my USB
objects.text: U1. Kim copies a report to a USB stick on every second work use at her PC. Her PC's policy blocks USB storage, so the copy is refused: she grumbles and emails the file to herself instead. The refusal counts as a failed work use, and her next social media post says IT blocked her USB, a hint that this PC is locked down.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Kim's PC
objects.observations: Kim's PC, under a policy that blocks USB storage.
objects.requiresItemHint: You would need a stick for this.

objects.name: Stick dock
objects.observations: A dock that takes a stick.
objects.requiresItemHint: You would need a stick for this.

itemsHeld.name: Kim's USB stick
itemsHeld.observations: A plain USB memory stick. Kim copies her work to it.

posts.text: Desk plant survived the weekend. Small victories.
IT blocked my USB stick again. Had to email the report to myself like it's 2005.

objects.name: Sign: F15 Three colleagues, one complaint
objects.text: F15. The project drive is down from the start. Asha, Kofi and Mei each try to work, fail, then pick up their phones. Whoever posts first vents; the other two reply in that thread instead of venting too. Stand back and watch the Friendface feed.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Asha's PC
objects.observations: Asha's PC, on the project drive.

objects.name: Kofi's PC
objects.observations: Kofi's PC, on the project drive.

objects.name: Mei's PC
objects.observations: Mei's PC, on the project drive.

posts.text: Project drive down again. Nothing will save today.
{name}, mine too. Has anyone rung IT about it?
Project drive is down and my files will not open.
{name}, same on my desk. Not one file will open.
No project drive this morning, so no work either.
{name}, mine is down as well. I have rung IT twice.

objects.name: Sign: F16 A pair, an answer and a second reply
objects.text: F16. The shared drive is down from the start. Ivy posts first and Tomasz replies in her thread. Later Ivy answers him there, and after that Tomasz replies once more. Stand back and watch for about two minutes.
objects.observations: A beat sign on a stand.

objects.name: Tomasz's PC
objects.observations: Tomasz's PC, on the shared drive.

objects.name: Ivy's PC
objects.observations: Ivy's PC, on the shared drive.

posts.text: Shared drive has gone. Lovely start to the week.
Same here {name}, I lost my whole morning.
Still no shared drive. I have given up for today.
{name}, they told me tomorrow at the earliest.
Shared drive down. Again. Nothing saves at all.
Not just you then, {name}. Mine has gone as well.
Two hours on and the drive is still down.
{name}, did IT ever ring you back about it?

contents.text: F5 done: a password built from two of Jake's posts and the IT poster opened his desktop.
